gaps.sentence: I ___ rather stay at home tonight, if that is all right.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather' expresses preference: would rather stay.

gaps.sentence: We ___ have hurried — the concert was cancelled anyway.
gaps.hint: the rush turned out to be unnecessary
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have hurried' means we hurried although it was unnecessary: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better book now — the prices rise every week.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' gives strong advice, often with urgency: had better book.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather not comment until the investigation is over.
gaps.hint: a polite refusal with would rather not
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather not' declines politely: would rather not.

gaps.sentence: He ___ have driven so fast on that icy road — he is lucky to be unhurt.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' criticizes dangerous past behavior: shouldn't have.

gaps.sentence: ___ I borrow your charger for a minute?
gaps.explanation: 'May' is the polite way to ask permission: May I borrow.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ to leave the gallery by 6 p.m.
gaps.hint: have to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' takes the full infinitive with 'to': have to leave.

gaps.sentence: Luckily I ___ find a parking space right outside the theatre.
gaps.hint: one particular success on that occasion
gaps.explanation: One particular success takes 'was able to': was able to find.
